reasoning: The parent <section> at line 35 only has className="relative min-h-[100dvh] w-full..." and is MISSING both `flex` and `flex-col`. The hero bottom bar at line 125 uses `mt-auto` which requires a flex column parent to push the element to the bottom of the flex container. Additionally, the <motion.div> at line 71 uses `my-auto` which also requires a flex parent for vertical centering. Since neither flex utility exists on the <section>, (a) the motion.div content is NOT vertically centered (my-auto is a no-op in block layout), and (b) `mt-auto` on the hero bottom bar does nothing — the bottom bar simply flows after the buttons in normal document flow rather than sitting flush with the bottom of the 100dvh viewport. Tracing the parent chain: <section> (block, NOT flex) → <motion.div> (content) + <div hero-bottom> (siblings in block flow). There is NO flex column wrapper between <section> and these two children that would make mt-auto work. This is a real, high-severity layout failure: the hero will not have its bottom bar anchored to the viewport bottom on any screen size, and the content will not be vertically centered.

At 320px iPhone SE width, the h2 uses text-[clamp(2rem,10vw,6.6rem)] (no sm override wins yet since 320px < 640px). 10vw of 320px = 32px = 2rem, so the clamp minimum wins and font-size is exactly 2rem/32px. The container is a single-column grid with horizontal section padding — roughly 288–300px of inner width. Line 34 "than digital clutter." is 21 uppercase characters. With the Syne display font (uppercase glyphs average ~0.6em width each) plus tracking-[-.065em], the estimated rendered width of this line is ~340–370px which exceeds the ~288–300px available. This line WILL wrap to an unexpected 4th line, breaking the designed 3-line composition. Separately, leading-[0.85] at 32px font gives a line-height of 27.2px — smaller than the font-size itself. All-caps Syne glyphs occupy roughly 0.75em (≈24px), leaving only ~3.2px of gap between consecutive lines. While pure uppercase avoids descender→ascender collision in the strict sense, the gap is razor-thin and the surprise 4th line makes the heading visually cramped and far denser than the 3-line design intended. This is a real bug at narrow mobile widths.

On a 568px-tall iPhone 5/SE viewport, the natural stacked height of all hero elements (using block flow because flex is absent — see issue 1) exceeds the viewport. Breakdown (approximate, using Tailwind's rem-based spacing at 16px root): pt-20 (80px) + SectionLabel (~20px) + h1 mt-8 (32px) + 3 headline lines at leading-[0.9] × clamp-min 1.85rem = 29.6px → 3 × 26.6px ≈ 80px + h1 mb-6 (24px) + p (3 lines, leading-relaxed × text-base 16px → ~78px) + p mb-10 (40px) + stacked buttons (min-h-11 each on <390px width → 44px + 3px gap + 44px ≈ 91px) + buttons mb-8 (32px) + hero bottom bar (~55px) + pb-16 (64px) ≈ 596px total. 596px > 568px, so the section (with min-h-[100dvh], not h-[100dvh]) grows and the user must scroll to see the very bottom padding and the full bottom bar. The three headline lines themselves (only ~80px) do NOT get clipped vertically — the headline text is fully visible. The issue is that the whole composition does not fit above-the-fold on a 568px viewport. Compounded by issue 1 (no flex column), the mt-auto on the bottom bar is not pushing it down anyway, so there is no "anchor to bottom" compression happening. Severity is low because the headline text itself is readable; only the above-the-fold expectation fails on very short devices.

The specific sm-breakpoint arithmetic the user described ("6 columns needed but sm:grid-cols-2") reflects a misunderstanding of CSS Grid: column spans do not need to sum to grid-cols-N in a single row because items automatically wrap to new rows. On sm (640–1023px) with sm:grid-cols-2, the layout is perfectly valid: Row 1 = Logo (col-span-2, full width), Row 2 = Company (1) | Services (1), Row 3 = Work (1) | Contact (1) — exactly 6 total column-spans across 3 rows of 2, zero wrapping issues on sm. However, there is a real col-span mismatch at the XS breakpoint (<640px) that the user's concern hints at but flagged the wrong breakpoint for. The logo column at line 83 uses unqualified `col-span-2 lg:col-span-2`, meaning col-span-2 applies STARTING AT THE DEFAULT/XS breakpoint. But the grid at xs (<640px) is only `grid-cols-1` (1 explicit column). When a col-span-2 item is placed in a 1-explicit-column grid, CSS Grid implicitly creates a 2nd column (governed by grid-auto-columns:auto, the browser default). This implicit 2nd column is present for all subsequent rows even though no other item spans into it, meaning Company/Services/Work/Contact (each col-span-1) get squeezed into column 1 (roughly 50% of grid width when the implicit column has non-zero size from the logo row) instead of occupying 100% width each. The predictable correct fix is `col-span-1 sm:col-span-2 lg:col-span-2` on the logo column. So the underlying col-span/config issue EXISTS, but the affected breakpoint is xs, not sm.
